interpretation_notes: Each boundary marker separates two proposed word-like or meaningful units.
Read a marked string such as Donne¦-¦le¦-¦moi as the proposed units Donne, -, le, -, moi.
Spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and punctuation can be separate units; do not reject an example merely because these separators have been split out.
Deterministic validation has already checked that removing the boundary markers recreates the input exactly.

review.strongest_reason: hyphenated preposition fused as a single -à- unit
review.explanation: Treating “-à-” as one unit hides the meaningful preposition à and suggests a non-existent morpheme. For learners, the hyphens should be separators and à should stand alone. Also, per guidance, the clitic split is clearer as C¦'est.
notes: Fixed expression is fine to segment internally if pieces remain transparent.
Apostrophe typically stays with the following piece: C¦'est.
Separating hyphens clarifies structure without inventing false chunks.
